neighbours.label: Directional particle or preposition right after a verb of moving or pouring something (pour gasoline onto, flow back into, give up), vs the same nouns without the motion phrase
fire: During the riot, someone tried to pour petrol onto the burning car.
If the valve fails, sewage can flow back into the kitchen sink.
After the scandal, the senator chose to give up his seat in March.
Each spring, melted snow will pour down onto the valley farms.
When the pump stops, the oil starts to flow back into the tank.
The coach told the players never to give up during a match.
Angry fans began to throw bottles onto the pitch after the goal.
Heavy rain made the muddy water spill over into the cellar.
quiet: During the riot, someone tried to photograph the burning car.
If the valve fails, the kitchen sink will need a new part.
After the scandal, the senator kept his seat until March.
Each spring, the valley farms hire extra workers for planting.
When the pump stops, the oil level in the tank stays the same.
The coach told the players to arrive early for each match.
Angry fans began to chant loudly in the stands after the goal.
Heavy rain made the muddy cellar smell damp for a week.
